items.summary: This document announces the availability of applicability determinations, regulatory interpretations, alternative monitoring, and other determinations made by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) from June 2025 to July 2026. The EPA made these applicability determinations, regulatory interpretations, alternative monitoring, and other determinations in response to inquiries concerning compliance with the Clean Air Act (CAA) stationary source program, specifically the New Source Performance Standards (NSPS); the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP); and the Emission Guidelines and Federal Plan Requirements for existing sources. The EPA posted the decisions on the CAA Section 111, 112, and 129 Applicability Determination Dashboard (ADD). This document also announces six broadly applicable alternative test method approval decisions that the EPA made in 2022, 2024, and 2025. These broadly applicable alternative test methods were approved in support of the NSPS and the NESHAP.
items.title: Additions to the Clean Air Act Section 111, 112, and 129 Applicability Determination Dashboard and to the List of Broadly Applicable Alternative Test Methods

items.summary: This regulation establishes exemptions from the requirement of a tolerance for residues of dimethyl sulfoxide (CAS Reg. No. 67-68-5) when used as an inert ingredient (solvent/cosolvent) in pesticide formulations applied to growing crops or to raw agricultural commodities after harvest, in pesticide formulations applied to animals, and in antimicrobial formulations applied to food-contact surfaces in public eating places, dairy-processing equipment, and food- processing equipment and utensils. Spring Regulatory Sciences on behalf of Gaylord Chemical Company, LLC submitted a petition to EPA under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA), requesting establishment of exemptions from the requirement of a tolerance. This regulation eliminates the need to establish maximum permissible levels for residues of dimethyl sulfoxide when used in accordance with the terms of those exemptions.
items.title: Dimethyl Sulfoxide in Pesticide Formulations; Exemptions From the Requirement of a Tolerance

items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a revised draft guidance for industry entitled "Essential Drug Delivery Performance Characteristics for Devices Intended to Deliver Drugs and Biological Products." This revised draft guidance revises and replaces the draft guidance entitled "Essential Drug Delivery Outputs Intended to Deliver Drugs and Biological Products" announced in the Federal Register on July 1, 2024 (89 FR 54470). In accordance with its mission of protecting, promoting, and advancing public health, this guidance addresses key aspects of drug delivery performance information for devices, and combination products that include device constituent parts, intended for delivery of a human drug, including a biological product (herein referred to as drug delivery devices). This guidance provides recommendations for development and organization of device drug-delivery performance information and data to improve the consistency of this information in applications and to facilitate transparency and predictability in development and regulatory review. The guidance is intended to facilitate and streamline development and lifecycle management of drug delivery devices.

items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is classifying the over-the-counter device to assess risk of sleep apnea into class II (special controls). The special controls that apply to the device type are identified in this order and will be part of the codified language for classification of the over-the-counter device to assess risk of sleep apnea. We are taking this action because we have determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of the safety and effectiveness of the device. We believe this action will also enhance patients' access to beneficial innovative devices, in part by reducing regulatory burdens.
items.title: Medical Devices; Anesthesiology Devices; Classification of the Over-the-Counter Device To Assess Risk of Sleep Apnea

items.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), a component of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), announces the issuance of an Amended Order under Sections 361, 365, 368, and 369 of the Public Health Service Act, and associated implementing regulations, prohibiting the boarding of any person who is not otherwise subject to an exemption on any aircraft destined to the United States from a foreign country unless the person presents a signed attestation confirming the person has not been present in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) during the 21 days prior to boarding a flight to the United States. This Amended Order was issued on October 28, 2026, to become effective at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on November 3, 2026, and shall remain in effect through 11:59 p.m. EST on December 18, 2026. This Amended Order may be amended or rescinded prior to that time at the discretion of the Secretary or his designee.
